trials.notes: Used the correct WP_HTML_Tag_Processor for a flat, position-based class edit. All called methods are documented: constructor, next_tag, set_bookmark, has_bookmark, seek, add_class, release_bookmark, get_updated_html. This is the documented bookmark idiom for remembering the last matching tag and then applying add_class before get_updated_html.

All API calls are documented and the frozen tests pass, but it chose WP_HTML_Processor for a flat tag/class mutation where the docs direct users to WP_HTML_Tag_Processor. The explanation incorrectly treats document-order scanning as requiring the structural parser. The is_tag_closer guard is unnecessary because documented next_tag defaults to openers only. It also does not check get_last_error after using the HTML Processor, so unsupported markup can stop the scan before a later H2.

All API calls are documented and the bookmark/add_class/get_updated_html pattern is mostly idiomatic. The main adherence issue is processor choice: WP_HTML_Processor is overpowered and less robust for this flat byte-preserving edit. create_full_parser-first is also a weak fit for unknown document-or-fragment input, especially when the task does not need structural parsing.

failure_analysis:
No frozen hidden cases failed in any trial: all three passed two-headings, single-heading, no-headings-unchanged, many-headings, comment-h2-not-counted, and existing-class.

The docs did well on the core path. The Tag Processor overview says to use it for flat, position-based work such as finding tags and changing classes. The next_tag docs explain forward-only scanning and the bookmark exception. The set_bookmark docs explicitly describe the supported idiom for remembering the last matching item by re-setting the same bookmark name in a loop. The add_class docs explain preserving existing classes and appending the new one, which covers the existing-class case. get_updated_html explains byte-preserving output for untouched input.

The near miss is processor selection. Trials 2 and 3 used WP_HTML_Processor because they overread 'document order' as a structural requirement. The HTML Processor docs do warn that it aborts on unsupported markup and that the Tag Processor suffices for flat attribute/class edits, but that warning did not prevent the misconception. A read-only probe showed the risk: with unsupported table fostering before a later H2, the reference Tag Processor still marks the later H2, while the HTML Processor versions fail to make the edit and emit warnings around seek. Trial 2 also missed the next_tag detail that tag closers are skipped by default, although this did not affect the frozen cases.

doc_gaps.problem: The correct 'last matching tag' pattern is present but buried in the set_bookmark method docs and uses a list example, so models may not connect it to simple flat mutations.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short general recipe near Usage: scan with next_tag for a tag/class query, re-set one literal bookmark on every match, seek once after the loop, mutate, then return get_updated_html. Keep it generic, not task-specific.

doc_gaps.location: Processor choice guidance in both class overviews
doc_gaps.problem: Some subjects interpreted whole-document order as requiring WP_HTML_Processor, despite the task only needing lexical tag order and a class edit.
doc_gaps.suggestion: State explicitly that document-order scans for first/last matching tags are still flat Tag Processor work unless the query depends on ancestors, depth, implied tags, subtree text, or normalized serialization.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs say fragment parsing is likely more appropriate unless sending an entire document, but they do not call out that full-parser-first fallback is usually the wrong shape for generic fragment-or-document class edits.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add guidance: when the operation does not need tree semantics, use WP_HTML_Tag_Processor for both documents and fragments; when tree semantics are needed and the input is ordinary post/body markup, prefer create_fragment() rather than probing create_full_parser() first.

doc_gaps.problem: Trial 2 added an unnecessary is_tag_closer guard after next_tag('h2'), suggesting the default closer behavior was not retained.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a compact opener-only example after the query table showing that next_tag('TAG') visits only openers unless tag_closers => 'visit' is supplied.

doc_gaps.location: WP_HTML_Processor unsupported-markup docs and bookmark/seek docs
doc_gaps.problem: The abort behavior is documented, but the practical consequence for mutation scans is easy to miss: after an abort, a previously-set bookmark may not be a safe basis for applying a best-effort edit unless the caller has checked get_last_error and chosen a fallback policy.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a mutation-scan note: after any HTML Processor scan that may encounter unsupported markup, check get_last_error before seeking back and mutating; for byte-preserving flat edits, prefer Tag Processor to avoid this abort surface.
